clips.send: Ernest Rutherford. Nuclear model. An atom is mostly empty space, with a tiny, dense, positive nucleus at the center. Electrons move around outside it. Gold-foil experiment: most alpha particles went straight through, but a few bounced back. Try the simulation below!

clips.send: J. J. Thomson. Plum-pudding model. Thomson discovered the electron. He pictured the atom as a ball of positive “pudding” with negative electrons stuck in it like raisins. Cathode-ray experiments: beams of tiny negative particles bent toward a positive plate.

clips.send: Big lesson: A model is not “wrong” for being replaced. Each model explained the evidence of its time, until new evidence demanded a better one.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Protons never jump between atoms in chemical reactions. Only electrons move. Changing protons is a nuclear change.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Protons never jump between atoms in chemical reactions. Only electrons move. Changing protons is a nuclear change.

clips.send: Neutron. Neutral (0) particle in the nucleus. Charge: 0. Mass: about 1 amu (a tiny bit heavier than a proton). Neutrons help hold the nucleus together. Without them, the positive protons would push each other apart. Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons are called isotopes.
clips.text: Neutron. Neutral (0) particle in the nucleus. Charge: 0. Mass: about 1 amu (a tiny bit heavier than a proton).. Neutrons help hold the nucleus together. Without them, the positive protons would push each other apart.. Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons are called isotopes.

clips.send: Nucleus. The tiny, heavy center of the atom. Made of protons and neutrons packed tightly together. Holds more than 99.9 percent of the atom’s mass, but only a tiny part of its volume. If an atom were the size of a football stadium, the nucleus would be about the size of a pea at the center. The nucleus has a positive charge because of its protons.

clips.send: Electron. Negative ( minus 1) particle around the nucleus. Charge: minus 1. Mass: about 1 over 1836 of a proton, so it barely counts toward the mass. Electrons are arranged in shells (energy levels) around the nucleus. In a neutral atom, the number of electrons equals the number of protons. Electrons in the outermost shell (valence electrons) take part in chemical reactions.

clips.send: Atomic number. equals number of protons. Every element has its own atomic number: H is 1, C is 6, O is 8. The periodic table is arranged in order of atomic number. In a neutral atom, it also equals the number of electrons.

clips.send: Niels Bohr. Bohr (shell) model. Electrons travel in fixed shells (energy levels) at set distances from the nucleus. They jump between levels when they absorb or give off energy. Each element gives off light of only certain colors (its line spectrum).

clips.send: Common mix-up: Adding neutrons does NOT change the element. It only changes the mass (and maybe the stability).
clips.text: Common mix-up: Adding neutrons does NOT change the element. It only changes the mass (and maybe the stability).

clips.send: Common mix-up: Ions form by gaining or losing ELECTRONS, never protons. Changing protons would change the element!
clips.text: Common mix-up: Ions form by gaining or losing ELECTRONS, never protons. Changing protons would change the element!

clips.send: Common mix-up: An atom’s nucleus and a cell’s nucleus are completely different things. They just share the name (“center”).
clips.text: Common mix-up: An atom’s nucleus and a cell’s nucleus are completely different things. They just share the name (“center”).

clips.send: Mass number. equals protons + neutrons. Electrons are so light that we don’t count them. Neutrons equals mass number minus atomic number. Example: carbon-14 has 14 minus 6 equals 8 neutrons. The number after an element’s name (carbon-12) is its mass number.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Atomic number counts PROTONS, not electrons. An ion has a different number of electrons but the same atomic number.

clips.send: Common mix-up: The third shell can actually hold 18 electrons, but for the first 20 elements it holds 8 before the fourth shell starts.
clips.text: Common mix-up: The third shell can actually hold 18 electrons, but for the first 20 elements it holds 8 before the fourth shell starts.

clips.send: Schrödinger and others. Electron-cloud (quantum) model. Electrons do not follow exact paths. We can only say where they are likely to be: a fuzzy electron cloud. In 1932 Chadwick discovered the neutron, completing today’s picture. Experiments showed that electrons behave like waves as well as particles.

clips.send: Electron shell. Energy levels where electrons are found. For elements 1–20: shell 1 holds up to 2 electrons, shell 2 up to 8, shell 3 up to 8 (the 2-8-8 rule). Electrons fill the inner shells first, then move outward. Atoms with a full outer shell (like helium, neon and argon) are very stable and unreactive.

clips.send: Proton. Positive (+1) particle in the nucleus. Charge: +1. Mass: about 1 atomic mass unit (amu). The number of protons is the atomic number, and it decides WHICH element the atom is. Add or remove one proton and the atom becomes a different element. Try it!

clips.send: Electron cloud. Today’s model: where electrons are LIKELY to be. Scientists cannot know exactly where an electron is at any moment, only where it is likely to be. Where the cloud is thicker, the electron is more likely to be found. This quantum (cloud) model came from scientists such as Schrödinger in the 1920s.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Isotopes of an element have the SAME chemical behavior, because they have the same electrons.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Mass number (a whole number for one atom) is different from the atomic mass on the periodic table (a decimal average of all isotopes).
clips.text: Common mix-up: Mass number (a whole number for one atom) is different from the atomic mass on the periodic table (a decimal average of all isotopes).

clips.send: Ion. An atom with unequal protons and electrons. Lose electrons, more protons than electrons, positive ion (cation), e.g. Na⁺. Gain electrons, more electrons than protons, negative ion (anion), e.g. Cl⁻. Table salt is made of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions held together.
clips.text: Ion. An atom with unequal protons and electrons. Lose electrons → more protons than electrons → positive ion (cation), e.g. Na⁺.. Gain electrons → more electrons than protons → negative ion (anion), e.g. Cl⁻.. Table salt is made of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions held together.

clips.send: Isotope. Same protons, different neutrons. Carbon-12, carbon-13 and carbon-14 are all carbon: each has 6 protons. Some isotopes are radioactive (unstable). Carbon-14 is used to find the age of things that were once alive, up to about 50,000 years old. Hydrogen has three isotopes: protium (0 n), deuterium (1 n) and tritium (2 n).

clips.send: Democritus. “Atomos”: uncuttable bits. Matter is made of tiny pieces that cannot be cut any smaller. He called them atomos, meaning “uncuttable”. No experiments. It was an idea based only on reasoning.

clips.send: John Dalton. Solid-sphere model. Atoms are tiny, solid, unbreakable balls. All atoms of one element are identical, and atoms join in whole-number ratios to form compounds. Elements always combined in fixed mass ratios when forming compounds.

clips.send: 电子云。现代模型：电子“可能”出现的区域。科学家无法确定电子某一时刻的准确位置，只能知道它在哪里出现的可能性大。电子云越密的地方，电子出现的机会越大。这种量子（电子云）模型来自 20 世纪 20 年代薛定谔等科学家的研究。

clips.send: 同位素。质子数相同、中子数不同。碳-12、碳-13 和碳-14 都是碳，都有 6 个质子。有些同位素具有放射性（不稳定）。碳-14 可以用来测定古代生物遗骸的年代（最多约 5 万年）。氢有三种同位素：氕（0 个中子）、氘（1 个中子）和氚（2 个中子）。

clips.send: 薛定谔等。电子云（量子）模型。电子没有确定的轨道，我们只能描述它们“可能”出现的区域，即电子云。1932 年查德威克发现了中子，完善了今天的原子图景。实验表明，电子既有粒子的性质，也有波的性质。

clips.send: 电子。在原子核外运动、带负电（减1）的粒子。电荷：减1。质量约为质子的 1836分之1，几乎可以忽略。电子分层排布在原子核外的电子层（能级）上。在不带电的原子中，电子数等于质子数。最外层电子（价电子）参与化学反应。

clips.send: 电子层。电子所在的能级。对前 20 号元素：第 1 层最多 2 个电子，第 2 层最多 8 个，第 3 层最多 8 个（“2-8-8”规律）。电子先填满内层，再排到外层。最外层“排满”的原子（如氦、氖、氩）非常稳定，几乎不发生反应。

clips.send: 原子核。原子中心又小又重的核心。由紧密挤在一起的质子和中子构成。原子 百分之99.9 以上的质量都在原子核里，但它只占原子体积的极小一部分。如果原子有足球场那么大，原子核只有场地中央的一颗豌豆那么大。因为含有质子，原子核带正电。

clips.send: 道尔顿。实心球模型。原子是微小、坚硬、不可分割的实心球。同种元素的原子都相同，不同原子按简单整数比结合成化合物。元素形成化合物时，总是按固定的质量比结合。

clips.send: 质量数。等于 质子数 + 中子数。电子太轻，不计入质量数。中子数 等于 质量数减原子序数。例如碳-14 有 14减6 等于 8 个中子。元素名称后面的数字（如碳-12）就是质量数。

clips.send: 原子序数。等于 质子数。每种元素都有自己的原子序数：氢是 1，碳是 6，氧是 8。元素周期表按原子序数的顺序排列。在不带电的原子中，它也等于电子数。

clips.send: 质子。原子核中带正电（+1）的粒子。电荷：+1。相对质量约为 1。质子数就是原子序数，它决定了原子是“哪一种”元素。增加或减少一个质子，原子就变成了另一种元素。试试看！

clips.text: 容易混淆：离子是通过得失“电子”形成的，不是得失质子。改变质子数就变成另一种元素了！

clips.send: 离子。质子数与电子数不相等的原子。失去电子，质子多于电子，带正电的阳离子，如 Na⁺。得到电子，电子多于质子，带负电的阴离子，如 Cl⁻。食盐（氯化钠）就是由 Na⁺ 和 Cl⁻ 结合而成的。
clips.text: 离子. 质子数与电子数不相等的原子. 失去电子 → 质子多于电子 → 带正电的阳离子，如 Na⁺。. 得到电子 → 电子多于质子 → 带负电的阴离子，如 Cl⁻。. 食盐（氯化钠）就是由 Na⁺ 和 Cl⁻ 结合而成的。

clips.send: 玻尔。玻尔模型（分层模型）。电子在离原子核一定距离的固定电子层（能级）上运动，吸收或放出能量时会在能级之间跃迁。每种元素只发出几种特定颜色的光（线状光谱）。
clips.text: 玻尔. 玻尔模型（分层模型）. 电子在离原子核一定距离的固定电子层（能级）上运动，吸收或放出能量时会在能级之间跃迁。. 每种元素只发出几种特定颜色的光（线状光谱）。
